candidate: fashion trend commentary -> recreate with owned wardrobe -> saved personal state -> repeat use

evidence.finding: For women in their teens through 50s, Instagram is the leading or tied-leading fashion information source; for men in their teens through 50s, YouTube is the leading source. TikTok is also material among people in their 20s.

Survey of 614 people reported movement from aspiration/trend-following toward finding a personal optimum; AI use emerged as a new fashion information source and SNS overload/trust concerns were reported as friction.

evidence.source: Hakuhodo Institute of Shopping Behavior 2026 AI Shopper survey
evidence.finding: Among a 20,000-person national sample, generative AI is increasingly used for shopping comparison, organization and advice, and many respondents want AI involved in final purchase decisions.

Even as some consumers are willing to delegate purchases to AI, clothing remains a category many want to choose themselves because it expresses identity and taste. This supports human taste plus AI assistance rather than full automation.

An AI stylist/closet product with millions of claimed users exists, showing that digital wardrobe plus outfit recommendation is an active market but also that generic AI stylist functionality is not a moat.
Fashion discovery on Instagram is shifting toward personality, authenticity, community and Reels; human taste remains important alongside rising AI use.

why: Fashion discovery is demonstrably social/video-led for large age segments in Japan.
Consumers increasingly want a personal optimum rather than more undifferentiated trend content.
AI is becoming acceptable in shopping assistance, while clothing still retains strong identity/taste involvement.
Existing closet/styling competitors validate demand but also invalidate generic AI stylist as sufficient differentiation.
what_is_not_proven: No evidence yet proves this exact product concept will retain users.
No evidence yet proves users will upload enough wardrobe items to create useful state.
No evidence yet proves willingness to pay for this exact wedge.
No evidence yet proves creator-character commentary materially improves conversion.
No evidence yet proves CAC, contribution margin or organic loop economics.

hundred_user_wedge.name: TREND_TO_MY_CLOSET
hundred_user_wedge.promise: See a trend, get an honest character-led verdict, then recreate or reject it using clothes you already own.
owned_state: context history such as work/casual/weather only when user-provided or first-party and appropriate
hundred_user_wedge.why_not_generic_ai_stylist: The differentiator is not outfit generation alone; it is the repeated loop from social trend commentary to the user's actual closet and accumulated decision history.
first_metrics: first useful answer -> at least one wardrobe item/state saved
active user -> share or organic referral
percentage of sessions users say could be fully replaced by generic AI
hundred_user_wedge.promotion_rule: Do not promote because of views or followers. Promotion requires evidence of repeat use and state-dependent value among the first 100 users.
kill_or_redesign_triggers: users refuse wardrobe/state setup at a rate that prevents first value
7-day return remains weak after setup friction is minimized
generic AI answers are judged equivalent for most sessions
manual owner workload scales materially with each user
acquisition depends on one fragile platform mechanic
privacy/policy requirements make the intended personalization impractical
